newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks seen mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks seen mixed in slow trading.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are seen mixed in slow trading on Thursday on expected continued profit-taking in blue-chips and local speculative buying of small-capitalised stocks, brokers said.
"Players are likely to continue taking profit as I don't seee any major news which could boost the market," one broker said.
Brokers said Wednesday's announcements of the country's latest inflation and trade surplus figures were within expectations and were not likely to have much impact on the market.
Newly-listed ceramics maker Intikeramik was likely to remain active after a strong debut on Wednesday, brokers said.
Brokers said profit-taking was likely to remain in blue-chips including Telkom, Bimantara and Bank BNI after recent strong gains.
On Wednesday, the Jakarta composite index fell 4.86 points, or 0.70 percent, to close at 693.54 points.
Astra fell 175 rupiah to 6,750 rupiah, with some 212,500 shares traded.

Another conglomerate with automotive interests, Bimantara, however, rose 50 rupiah to 3,900 rupiah as the firm's total revenue was not considered to be too dependent on its automotive division, brokers said.
Bank BNI topped the active list, with some nine million shares traded but brokers said the reasons for the active trading were not clear.
